issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution repository introduces a different interface named 'Mountable' and leaves Rideable.java empty. Pig and Seal in the solution implement Mountable instead of Rideable, while the template Main and UML in the problem refer to Rideable. This naming mismatch prevents students from following the specified design and will cause compilation/type errors if they try to use the template Main or follow the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the problem statement and template by implementing and using the 'Rideable' interface (with messageOnRide()) instead of introducing 'Mountable'. Either rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java and update the interface file contents accordingly, and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, or ensure Rideable.java in the solution contains the correct interface and remove the extraneous Mountable. This aligns solution, template, and UML nomenclature and avoids compile/type errors.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface (method messageOnRide()), but the solution implementation uses an interface named Mountable for the same concept. Additionally, Rideable.java in the solution is empty. This naming divergence (Rideable vs Mountable) for the same capability creates confusion mapping the requirement to the implementation and will mislead students when they try to implement or use the interface as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the Mountable interface (and its file) in the solution to Rideable and ensure it declares messageOnRide(); update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable. Alternatively, implement the Rideable interface in Rideable.java (with messageOnRide()) and have Mountable removed or made an alias to Rideable so that template/problem references and solution use the same identifier.
